pr_title: Enable provider-implemented sig algs for s_server startup
pr_body:
- Probes & sets external provider-delivered security bit information for certs with MD=NID_undef (e.g., quantum-safe certificates)
- Limits known signature algorithm assertions to known (i.e., non-external provider implemented) signature algorithms
  
Fixes #18375

issue_context.title: security bits set by ossl_x509_init_sig_info OK?
issue_context.body:
~Is the [code setting security bits for X509 cert info](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a4e21d18d5b7cb4fef66c10f13b1b3b55945439f/crypto/x509/x509_set.c#L195-L276) sufficiently robust for public key algorithms losing in strength over time? The code seems to assign "secbits" exclusively based on the strength of the message digest without taking the strength of the public key (algorithm) into account.~

~Wouldn't it be more suitable to initialize `siginf->secbits` by `EVP_PKEY_get_security_bits(X509_PUBKEY_get(x->cert_info.key))` and then reduce the value of `siginf->secbits` by the strength of the MD algorithm?~

I encountered this code when working on integrating provider-implemented signature algorithms (#10512): [ossl_x509_init_sig_info](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a4e21d18d5b7cb4fef66c10f13b1b3b55945439f/crypto/x509/x509_set.c#L273) proved to be not correctly handling such algorithms (ones doing their own digesting, i.e., with mdnid=NID_undef), so code to delegate setting "siginf->secbits" to a provider needed to be added:

Please see [this diff](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/compare/master...baentsch:sigprovider?expand=1) if there'd be agreement with the assessment and a PR would be desirable.

or is this somehow not working?

Thanks for the pointer: This looks good and explains things for me: The function above calls `ssl_security_cert_sig` which in turn retrieves the `secbits` set by the function `ossl_x509_init_sig_info` referenced above: In other words, `ossl_x509_init_sig_info` indeed only is meant to set `secbits` representing the MD (strength), not the full signature. This was my misunderstanding: I always consider MD and sig alg to be "one item".

So there's no problem with key strength checking (text above suitably edited) -- but still one setting `secbits` for signature algorithms that don't need a message digest (i.e., non-legacy, provider-based ones): Those should set "secbits" based on the strength of that "MD-incl-sig" algorithm and not bail/fail as per https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a4e21d18d5b7cb4fef66c10f13b1b3b55945439f/crypto/x509/x509_set.c#L216-L223

I'm slightly confused by this call. We've already called `OBJ_find_sigid_algs` to get the `mdnid` and `pknid` from the signature id. Now you seem to be calling `OBJ_find_sigid_by_algs` to go back the other way. Why? We know this will succeed because `OBJ_find_sigid_algs` was successful in the first place.
Should we handle the case where `EVP_PKEY_get_security_bits()` returns 0?
I'm not sure if the logic is quite right here. If a custom handler exists then we should probably honour its return code and fail. If it doesn't exist *then* we can go down this new code path.

This change is not correct. `i` here is an index into the pkeys array:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/dc0ef292f7df4ce0c49c64b47726a6768f9ac044/ssl/ssl_local.h#L2018

Each index corresponds to a difference certificate type:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/dc0ef292f7df4ce0c49c64b47726a6768f9ac044/ssl/ssl_local.h#L399-L408

You have initialised `i` to `SSL_aANY` and are using that value as a default in the case where there is no base id. But `SSL_aANY` isn't intended to be used as an index into pkeys. It's one of the auth types `SSL_a*`. These auth values are currently in the range 0 to 0x80.  As it happens `SSL_aANY` co-incidentally has a value of 0, which just happens to be a valid index corresponding to `SSL_PKEY_RSA`.

So this code will work - but only by accident because it pretends that the cert is actually an RSA cert.

> But SSL_aANY isn't intended to be used as an index into pkeys. 

Got it . Becomes clear when running the code, too. This requires many more changes, incl. SIGALG_LOOKUP logic (and table) and probably many more. Sorry for the premature PR.
